bundestag.summary:
SUMMARY:
This document is the stenographic report of the 78th session of the 21st legislative period of the German Bundestag, held on Friday, May 8, 2026. The agenda covered several key topics. A significant portion of the session was dedicated to the second and third readings of a government bill to introduce electronic monitoring of offenders and perpetrator work within the Protection against Violence Act. This bill was debated alongside a recommendation from the Committee on Legal Affairs and Consumer Protection regarding a motion by Die Linke for a comprehensive strategy against domestic and gender-based violence. Debates involved representatives from SPD, AfD, CDU/CSU, and BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN, with specific concerns raised by Aaron Valent (Die Linke) and contributions from Carmen Wegge (SPD), Rainer Galla (AfD), Dr. Günter Krings (CDU/CSU), and Dr. Lena Gumnior (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN). Federal Minister Dr. Stefanie Hubig (BMJV) also addressed the assembly.

Further agenda items included a first reading of an AfD bill to abolish the Wind Energy Area Requirement Act (WindBAG) and an AfD motion for a nationwide moratorium on wind energy expansion, leading to discussions involving Christian Reck (AfD), Dr. Maria-Lena Weiss (CDU/CSU), Katrin Uhlig (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN), Dr. Paul Schmidt (AfD), and Dunja Kreiser (SPD). The Bundestag also considered a joint motion by CDU/CSU and SPD on the "Tag der Städtebauförderung 2026" (Urban Development Funding Day). Additionally, Die Linke introduced several motions aimed at strengthening works council rights, improving their working conditions, promoting works council formations, and expanding employee participation, with speakers like Cem Ince (Die Linke) and Peter Aumer (CDU/CSU) participating. The session also touched upon strengthening co-determination at the multinational level through reforms of European Works Councils.

UKRAINIAN MEN:
No discussion about Ukrainian men found in this session.

facts.fact: During the reign of King Louis XIV of France, perfume became so essential to the court that the palace of Versailles had a dedicated 'Perfume Department.' The king bathed only once in his life, leading courtiers to douse themselves in potent scents to mask body odor, a practice that defined aristocratic fashion.

The tradition of wearing white at weddings, now a global custom, largely stems from Queen Victoria's choice of a white satin gown for her marriage to Prince Albert in 1840. Before this, brides often wore their best dress, regardless of color, as white was difficult to clean and symbolized wealth more than purity.
